item.title: Future Scholars in Business and Society: Current Work and Emerging Directions
item.content:encoded:
Barrie Litzky, Drexel University

This special issue of Business and Society Review seeks doctoral research exploring the relationship between business and society. The journal welcomes emerging scholarship that addresses ethical challenges, corporate responsibility, stakeholder relations, sustainability, and social innovation, as well as newer concerns like technology and artificial intelligence. The issue aims to provide doctoral students with a venue to present novel questions, perspectives, and methodological approaches that advance the field.

Submissions may be at various stages of development, from defended dissertation proposals to more advanced work with preliminary findings. Both empirical and conceptual studies are welcome. Manuscripts must be authored exclusively by doctoral students or teams of doctoral students, with faculty members limited to informal advisory roles. All submissions will undergo standard double-blind peer review and follow the journal's formatting guidelines.

Appel publié par Business and Society Review. Voir l'appel sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • Ethical decision-making and moral responsibility
  • Stakeholder theory and engagement
  • Inequality, precarity, and justice
  • Sustainability and social innovation
  • Technology, AI, and data ethics
  • Institutional and global perspectives on business-society issues
  • Corporate governance and responsibility
  • Business-government relations and policy
  • Conceptual and theoretical advancements
  • Pedagogical research in ethics and CSR
